answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, non-reusable stake before it may earn from a task, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence for free: every identity needs capital, and a detected fake loses its bond. A ripple of corroborated reports can trigger review, while a karst-like network of small accounts offers no haven if they share funding or behavior that links them to one operator.
